column2: On the authority of Abū Dharr Jundub ibn Junādah and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Muʿādh ibn Jabal (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with them both), from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:

“Fear Allah wherever you are; follow a bad deed with a good deed and it will wipe it out; and treat people with good character.” Reported by al-Tirmidhī, who said: “A ḥasan hadith”; in some copies: “ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ”.
With its three sentences, this hadith comprises what is required of a Muslim towards his Lord, himself and others.
His words, “Fear Allah wherever you are”: the root meaning of taqwā in the language is to place between oneself and what one fears a shield that protects one from it,
such as wearing sandals and leather socks for protection from harmful things on the ground, or taking houses and tents for protection from the heat of the sun, and so on. Taqwā in the Sharīʿah

is for a person to place between himself and the anger of Allah a shield that protects him from it, by doing what is commanded, leaving what is forbidden, believing the reports [of revelation], and worshipping Allah in accordance with the Sharīʿah, not with innovations and newly invented matters.

Fear of Allah is required in all circumstances, places and times: one fears Allah in secret and in public, when visible to people and when hidden from them, as has come in this hadith: “Fear Allah wherever you are.”

His words, “follow a bad deed with a good deed and it will wipe it out”: when a person commits a bad deed, he repents of it, and repentance is a good deed that wipes out what came before it, major and minor sins alike. It is also done by doing good deeds, for they wipe out minor sins; as for major sins, nothing wipes them out except repentance from them.
His words, “and treat people with good character”: a person is required to treat all people well, treating them as he would like them to treat him,
because he ﷺ said: “None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself,” and he ﷺ said:

“Whoever would love to be moved away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise, let his death come to him while he believes in Allah and the Last Day, and let him treat people the way he would love to be treated.”
Allah described His Prophet ﷺ as being of great character, and it has come from ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) that his ﷺ character was the Qurʾān,

reported by Muslim (746), meaning that he put into practice what it contains. Many hadiths have come in the Sunnah showing the virtue of good character, urging the adoption of good character traits and warning against bad ones.
The perfection of the Messenger's ﷺ sincere care for his nation, which includes the three great, comprehensive pieces of advice contained in this hadith.
The command to fear Allah in all circumstances, places and times.
Encouragement to follow bad deeds with good deeds.
Good deeds wipe out bad deeds.
Encouragement to treat people with good character.
